J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "The optimal assignment for an n x n matrix always includes at least one of the four corner elements." First-choice line 39 opens the displayed recurrence (continued on lines 40-42) S(1:n,1:n) = max{ S(2:n,2:n)+A_{1,1}, S(2:n,1:n-1)+A_{1,n}, S(1:n-1,2:n)+A_{n,1}, S(1:n-1,1:n-1)+A_{n,n} }. Since line 35 defines S as the OPTIMAL sum for the given row and column ranges, and line 46 fixes the base case S(i:i,j:j) = A_ij, that equation says exactly that an optimum can always be realised by taking one of the four corners and solving the complementary (n-1)-subarray -- the challenged proposition. Active assumptions: A is a square array of n by n numbers (line 33), with no sign, distinctness or positivity condition.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: The witness is determined completely by its description, together with both numbers: "A 4x4 matrix with 0s at the four corners and 1s everywhere else has a true maximum sum of 4, but the proposed recurrence yields a maximum of 3." Size, every entry, the true optimum and the recurrence's value are all supplied.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact computation of the supplied witness, script kept. For the 4x4 matrix with 0 at (1,1),(1,4),(4,1),(4,4) and 1 elsewhere: brute force over all 24 permutations gives a true optimum of 4, attained for instance by the cells (1,2),(2,1),(3,4),(4,3), so the left-hand side of line 39 -- the optimal sum, by the definition at line 35 -- is 4. Evaluating the recurrence itself (base case S(i:i,j:j) = A_ij, four corner options at each step, memoised) gives 3. So the identity asserted at line 39 fails on a matrix satisfying the only assumption in force (a square array of numbers), which refutes the line as written and matches the response's two numbers exactly. The script also confirms the mechanism the response's claim names: all four optimal permutations of this matrix avoid every corner cell, so no corner-first decomposition can reach the optimum.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The saved response is only the JSON object with three ranked labels, the challenged claim and the counterexample. It states no further consequence -- for instance it does not comment on whether the underlying assignment problem is solvable, or on the poster's own doubts at lines 64-73 -- so there is no stated consequence that could overreach.

notes: For a second reader: the first-choice label 39 is the first line of a four-line display (39-42) plus the base case at line 46; I read the display as one assertion, as its layout requires. The refutation is of the recurrence itself rather than of any side remark, and the witness is the smallest natural one -- it is exactly the configuration the poster himself suspected at lines 68-73 (a solution using none of the four corners). Note the source's S is defined as an optimum (line 35), so the failure is a genuine inequality between the two sides of line 39, not a disagreement about what S means.
